content.text:
Done. The fix, in three files:

**`lib/decorate.js`** — added `hasInstanceProperty(fn, name)`, which checks the constructor's `instanceProperties` set and walks the `parent` chain (derived constructors from `buildRequest`/`buildReply` don't own the set). It's now consulted by `decorateConstructor` (so `decorateRequest`/`decorateReply` throw `FST_ERR_DEC_ALREADY_PRESENT`) and by `checkRequestExistence`/`checkReplyExistence` (so `hasRequestDecorator`/`hasReplyDecorator` return `true`).

**`lib/request.js`** — `Request.instanceProperties = new Set(['id', 'params', 'raw', 'query', 'log', 'body'])`.

**`lib/reply.js`** — `Reply.instanceProperties = new Set(['raw', 'request', 'log'])`.

Co-change / hot-file notes from COMPLEX.md:
- `lib/request.js` ↔ `lib/reply.js` (38%): both needed the change, symmetrically — each got the set matching its own constructor body.
- `lib/reply.js` ↔ `lib/symbols.js` (52%): **no change needed** — `instanceProperties` covers only string-keyed constructor properties; no new symbol was introduced and the symbol-keyed reply state is untouched.
- Its guidance to "add or change getters in both builder paths" doesn't bite here: I added no getter. The sets live on the base constructors and both builder paths inherit them via the existing `Object.setPrototypeOf(_Request, R)` / `_Request.parent = R` (verified by the trustProxy case in the new tests), and the trust-proxy-only getters (`ip`, `ips`, `host`, `protocol`) are prototype-defined, so the pre-existing prototype checks already cover them.
- `fastify.js`, `lib/route.js`, `lib/errors.js` and `types/errors.d.ts`: untouched, no new error code or public instance property.

Tests: added `test/decorator-instance-properties.test.js` (6 node:test tests — detection, throwing, encapsulated + trustProxy contexts, and that ordinary decorators still work end-to-end); all 6 pass, and the existing `test/decorator.test.js` still passes all 52. Per your one-file limit I did not run the `test/diagnostics-channel/*.test.js` suite that the hot-file rules for `lib/reply.js`/`lib/request.js` ask for — that's 11 files; worth running before merge. Lint was not run (the `npx eslint` call needed approval). Nothing committed.
